courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Literacy Reflection
courses.description: Focuses on reflective literacy teaching: problematizing, processes of understanding students' thinking about reading and writing.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Assessment and Accountability
courses.description: Provides students with the opportunity to review, renew, and expand their understanding of assessment and program evaluation procedures, as well as the role of accountability in educational settings.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Reinventing Teaching
courses.description: Admission to the M.Ed. for experienced teachers program required. Addresses contexts of teaching, teaching in the world, and teaching students in schools. This course is designed for experienced educators to "reinvent teachers and teaching."

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Teacher Researcher I
courses.description: Enrollment in the M.Ed. for Experienced Teachers program required. Explores the meanings of research and the potential roles of teachers in conducting research. Teachers formulate possible individual or small group research projects that they can carry out during the year.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Teacher Researcher II
courses.description: Teachers will plan and conduct advanced inquiry/research projects informed by their knowledge of teacher-research and their experience as teacher-researchers garnered through their successful completion of EDMX 708 .

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Teacher Leadership for a Democratic Society
courses.description: Focuses on the nature of change and teachers' roles as leaders within a changing environment. Several themes are addressed: shaping school cultures, schools as communities, schools as sites for reform, and politics and schools.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Assessment and Differentiation
courses.description: Enrollment in the M.Ed. for experienced teachers program required. Enhances teachers' understanding of how to differentiate assessment.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Assessment and Differentiation
courses.description: Enrollment in the M.Ed. for experienced teachers program required. Enhances teachers' understanding of how to differentiate instruction. Using a case-based approach, teachers examine the areas of human development, special education and inclusion, cultural diversity, linguistic diversity, cognitive styles, and multiple intelligences as frames through which to consider creative environments to promote students' classroom success.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Content-Area Reading and Writing
courses.description: Focuses on current theory, research, and issues in the teaching and use of reading and writing in the content areas. This is an introductory course.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Advanced Reflective Literacy Teaching
courses.description: Teachers will learn how to problematize assessment of students' thinking about reading and writing in this practicum course.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Number Systems and Operations: K-5 Mathematical Tasks
courses.description: Course has major restrictions. Analysis and construction of effective mathematical tasks in teaching number systems and operations at the K-5 level; attention is also given to the expansion of content knowledge.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Data Analysis and Measurement: K-5 Classroom Interactions
courses.description: Course has major restrictions. Focuses on statistical literacy of elementary teachers and the teaching of data analysis and measurement to K-5 students; attention is also given to learning methods that facilitate appropriate classroom interactions.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Rational Numbers and Operations: K-5 Learning Trajectories
courses.description: Course has major restrictions. Focuses on rational number concepts through learning trajectories at the K-5 level. Attention also given to problem solving and content knowledge.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Revisiting Real Numbers Concepts
courses.description: Uses a problem-based format and group work to explore the mathematics of the real numbers with an emphasis on rational numbers.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Algebraic Reasoning: K-5 Discourse and Questioning
courses.description: Course has major restrictions. Focus on the early algebra concepts of functional thinking and generalized arithmetic in relationship to pedagogical practices centered on questioning in the mathematics classroom.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Topics in Mathematics Education: Geometry
courses.description: Provides students with a mathematical foundation and cognitive support for elementary and middle school geometry. Specific goals address structure of elementary and middle school geometry.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Geometry and Spatial Visualization: K-5 Assessment
courses.description: Course has major restrictions. Geometric concept development along with formative and summative assessment strategies of students' geometric thinking. Attention also is given to geometric content knowledge and diagnosis of student errors.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Writing in the 21st Century
courses.description: Focuses on the writing process and the theoretical foundations necessary to become practitioners who can develop and implement effective writing instruction using 21st-century skills.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Explorations in Literacy
courses.description: Explores what it means to be a reader and writer, the nature of development of literacy.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Spanish for Educators
courses.description: This graduate-level course is an introductory immersion-style Spanish course for anyone involved in education. Learners will acquire novice-level proficiency in Spanish and an awareness of Hispanic culture.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Revisiting Literacy
courses.description: Explores literacy topics as capstone course for master's or licensure program in literacy.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Math and Content Area Methods: Special Education, General Curriculum
courses.description: Students will learn characteristics of students with mild to moderate learning disabilities in math, social studies, and science. They will also learn assessment techniques and instructional methods to address these specific characteristics.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Mathematical Modeling: K-5 Leadership
courses.description: Restricted to majors. Generating mathematical representations and making explicit connections between concepts. Pedagogy designed to equip elementary teachers to become mathematics teacher-leaders in school settings. Focuses on topics integrated within mathematical strands.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Social Studies Pedagogy A
courses.description: Designed to extend students' professional content knowledge by exploring the content and methods of a social science discipline.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Social Studies Pedagogy B
courses.description: Designed to extend students' professional content knowledge by exploring the content and methods of a social science discipline.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Contemporary Research for Social Studies Teaching
courses.description: Focuses on current research topics and methodologies in the field of social studies education and examines their implications on the field.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Integrated Learning
courses.description: Builds on earlier coursework and will include teachers from each of the two concentrations in the M.Ed. for Experienced Teachers. It focuses on exploring what is meant by integrated curriculum and understanding the process of developmental research as it relates to the design and use of curricula.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Social Studies/Humanities
courses.description: Aims to develop social studies teachers' understanding of social science and humanities through an interdisciplinary inquiry process.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Advanced Emergent and Early Literacy
courses.description: Advanced course on emergent and early literacy, focusing on the research and theory in the development of reading and writing processes from birth through first grade, emphasizing the cognitive and socio-cultural perspectives.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Diversity Global Education
courses.description: Provides a linked perspective on international studies and multicultural education. Students explore issues relevant to these two topics as they relate to teaching and learning in social studies.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Families and Teams in Early Childhood Intervention: Interdisciplinary Perspectives
courses.description: Open to graduate students only. Explores issues and models of family-professional and interprofessional relationships in early childhood settings. Collaborative communication and problem-solving strategies are emphasized in the context of diversity.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Early Childhood Assessment Strategies
courses.description: Open to graduate students only. Provides an overview and application of strategies for developmental screenings, normative evaluations, curriculum, and play-based assessments for young children ages birth through five.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Preschool/Kindergarten Curriculum and Learning Environments
courses.description: Open to graduate students only. Focuses on individually, developmentally, and culturally appropriate learning environment and curriculum strategies for young children with and without disabilities ages three to five.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Infant/Toddler Curriculum and Learning Environment
courses.description: Focuses on infant/toddler development and mental health strategies for facilitating development in the home and in child care.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Professional Development and Leadership in Early Childhood Intervention
courses.description: Focuses on leadership skills in mentoring, supervision, staff development, resource gathering, and applied research related to early childhood settings.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Seminar in Science Education
courses.description: Teaches students curriculum and instruction strategies in science education. The focus of the course is on teaching and assessing science for conceptual understanding.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Perspectives on Science Education: Physical Science
courses.description: Examines physical science domains in depth. Students reflect on their own understandings of science phenomena and research their students' understandings.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Perspectives on Science Education: Life Science
courses.description: Studies the history of science education, curriculum design, and national reform ideas as well as projects and programs currently used in United States classrooms.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Perspectives of Science Education: Earth, Space, and Environmental Science
courses.description: Explores current reforms in science education through an examination of critical topics in earth-space science.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Big Ideas in Science Education
courses.description: Through investigations, research, and guest speakers, this course engages students in discussions about teaching science in conjunction with issues of technology and society.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Behavioral Support Techniques
courses.description: Emphasizes effective behavior management and applied behavior analysis techniques for intervening in the environments of exceptional children to increase learning.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Designing Problem Tasks for Mathematics
courses.description: Focuses on the analysis and construction of mathematics instructional activities.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Problem-Based Learning in Mathematics
courses.description: Focuses on the analysis and construction of mathematics instructional activities: tasks, problems, and materials with which students and teachers engage.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Developing Mathematical Knowledge
courses.description: Designed to help teachers think through the major mathematical ideas of the curriculum and to examine how students develop these ideas.

courses.subject: EDMX
courses.title: Culturally Responsive Teaching
courses.description: This course initiates thoughtful discussion of race and culture in our schools by exploring history, identity, and issues in academic achievement.
